paper.title: Real-Time, Continuous Level of Detail Rendering of Height Fields
paper.venue: Proceedings of the 23rd annual conference on Computer graphics and interactive techniques (SIGGRAPH 1996), pp. 109-118

relevant_section_or_figure: Section 3.1, Continuous Level of Detail; Section 4, Simplification Criteria; Figure 1, which compares terrain tessellations at projected geometric-error thresholds of one and four pixels.
transferable_principle: Drive geometry complexity from a continuous, user-controlled screen-space error budget rather than from raw world distance alone: select a coarse spatial LOD, refine locally only where projected deviation exceeds the pixel threshold, and transition continuously as the view changes.
application_to_world_v21: Partition terrain and decorative geometry into spatial blocks and assign each block a projected-error budget based on the active camera. Collapse distant low-salience clutter aggressively while retaining the broad terrain silhouette and a small set of scale landmarks. Give worker traces, task parcels, receipts, EON-time cues, and epistemic-state markers a separate minimum screen-size/readability floor so LOD can simplify their supporting geometry without erasing their meaning; use morphing or another continuous transition at threshold crossings to reduce popping during fly-throughs.
falsifier: The transfer is falsified if matched camera fly-throughs with a fixed screen-space budget produce no measurable reduction in clutter or improvement in perceived scale/readability at equal triangle cost, or if semantic state markers remain unreadable despite meeting their declared pixel floor. That result would show that this terrain-oriented error criterion is insufficient for World v21's semantic and cinematic demands.
